title: Rajasthan Vidhan Sabha, 9th Assembly, Session 6, proceedings 5 March 1992: Unstarred Q.243 and Q.247 (Mahajan Field Firing Range)
villages_named: chidasar (चीदासर, print unclear, could read बीदासर, p.77)
rina (रीणा, as alias of Raimalwali, p.78)
what_it_contains: Q.247 (Shri Maniram Siyag, Lunkaransar) answer by Revenue Minister: 'महाजन रेन्ज के कुल 33 गांव उठाये गये थे जो निम्न हैं' followed by a numbered list of 33 villages (printed pp.77-78). Compensation for agricultural land Rs 42,35,18,935.50; Rs 18,66,923.90 still unpaid; last payment 18-7-91 by SDO (North) Bikaner. Q.243 (Anang Kumar Jain) on panchayat compensation: all villages of Gram Panchayat Jagor acquired (Rs 1,10,33,744.90 deposited by challan 32 dt 11-3-88); three villages of GP Kanolai (Kanolai, Berawala and a third, OCR unclear) acquired, new GP Raner formed; four villages of GP Kumbhana (Kumbhana, Manera, Bhuwala, Ladera) acquired, new GP Bhikhnera formed; two villages of GP Kharbara (Chindasar, Devasar) acquired; FIRs 13,14,15 dt 26-2-92 at Chhatargarh and Mahajan police stations for misappropriation.
why_relevant: The only official, printed, named list of the 33 MFFR villages found so far. It equals the 32 revenue villages missing from the 1991 census plus Birmana (बीरमाना, #29). This settles which villages the state counts as '33'. Also shows old gram panchayat groupings.

title: Rajasthan Vidhan Sabha, 5th Assembly, 23 March 1974: Unstarred Q.326 'Villages being vacated for firing practice in Lunkaransar tehsil' and Appendix 8 (list of 32 villages)
villages_named: kanolai (चकरामपुरा = Chak Rampura, likely the Rampura bas of Kanolai, p.363)
what_it_contains: Q.326 by Shri Chunnilal Indaliya (Nokha): are many villages of Lunkaransar tehsil being vacated for 'chandmari'? Answer (p.59): 'बीकानेर जिले की तहसील लूणकरणसर के 32 ग्राम सेना द्वारा तोपाभ्यास के लिये अवाप्त का प्रस्ताव राज्य सरकार के विचाराधीन है'; compensation as per rules; some objections received. Appendix 8 (printed p.363) lists 32 names: Nakrasar, Kumasar, Meusar, Bhojrasar, Kakraliya, Jagor, Kanolai, Thoiyo, Kummana, Manera, Rina urf Raimalwali, Mahadevwali, Motasar, Ladera, Ladera (repeated), Bhunwala, Beermana, Musalki, Bijharwali, Lakhawar, Khileriya, Shobholai(?Shubhlai), Ajitmana, Karnali, Sadolai, Berawala, Kunda, Rajasar Bhatiyan, Khokhrana, Chak Rampura, Dhanasar, Machhwali Johdi.
why_relevant: Earliest official list found (1974) of villages proposed for the artillery range. It differs from the final 1992 list: it includes villages that were later left out (Mahadevwali, Musalki, Bijharwali, Lakhawar, Khileriya, Karnali, Sadolai, Kunda, Rajasar Bhatiyan, Khokhrana) and names Dhanasar and 'Machhwali Johdi' (Machhranwali) as separate places. So the range boundary was redrawn between 1974 and 1980-85. Explains why people remember different names and counts.

title: Khed Rapat (खेड़ रपट), Nanuram Sanskarta, Lok Sahitya Pratishthan, Kalu (Bikaner), 1st ed. 26 Jan 1984, 592 pp. (DLI title 'Khadai-rapat', creator given as Shiv Raj Sanskarta)
villages_named: rina (रिणो, merged into Raimalwali, p.454; रायमलवाला (रेणा) #135 p.453)
kanolai (कानालाई #134 p.453; चक रामपुरा बास in Kanolai p.454)
what_it_contains: Local history of Kalu and Lunkaransar tehsil in Hindi/Rajasthani. Key pages (image-verified): p.327 footnote 'मुटलाई आदि 34 गाँव फौज की छावनी बनाने बाबत खाली करवाये जा रहे हैं'; p.452-454 numbered list of all 171 villages of Lunkaransar tehsil (141 inhabited + 30 be-chirag), and a list of old villages absorbed into others, incl. 'चक रामपुरा बास (कानोलाई में), धनासर (कुम्भाणा में), माछरावाली (भोजरासर में), रिणो (रायमल वाली में), हजरत पुरा (दुदेर में)'; p.454 'उन्नीसवीं शताब्दी के मध्यकाल तक तहसील लूनकरनसर में 210 गाँव आबाद थे... 39 गाँव शून्य हो गए'; p.454 broad-gauge Suratgarh-Bikaner line for the cantonment begun at Mahajan station on 17.2.1983; p.485 the cantonment will be between the Rajasthan Canal and the Lunkaransar lift canal, north-west of Mahajan; p.489 'तहसील के 171 गावों में से कुंभाणा, मुटलाई, मणेरा आदि लगभग 30 गावों को उठाकर फौज की छावनी बनाने की सरकारी योजना है'; p.485 Kumbhana, Manera, Sulera, Bhikhnera, Bhuwala called 'Kachhas ke bas'; p.426 sub-health centre at Kanolai, family welfare sub-centre Motolai; p.428 26 panchayats incl. Kanolai, Kumbhana, Jagor; p.430 police chowki at Kumbhana; p.152 Major Puran Singh (Manera), Vir Chakra 1965; p.331/439 Thakur Bhupal Singh of Duder became Raja of Mahajan (1933).
why_relevant: A pre-displacement (1983-84) eyewitness local source. It names nearly all range villages, gives the '34 villages' figure in print in 1984, and places the 'lost' names: Machhranwali inside Bhojrasar, Dhannasar inside Kumbhana, Rina = Raimalwali, Rampura bas inside Kanolai.
found_via: archive.org FTS "खियाणा", "मुटलाई", "मेऊसर"; full PDF (15,084,986 bytes, sha256 3eff3d42251d095870549fccbc7b9106e59ccf2c96424f5024963d9b34c5e2c4) kept in scratchpad; IA OCR text saved as research/leads/files/history/khed_rapat_1984_ia_ocr_pages.txt; 1984 work, copyright likely with author's heirs: extract kept for research only

title: Bikaner, by Sarangadhar Das. Report submitted to the President, All India States Peoples' Conference (States Peoples' Conference New Series No.6); DLI copy dated 1935 (text refers to 1939 events); second copy 1940: https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.505610
what_it_contains: Appendix E (pp.129-132): 1939 memorial to the Maharaja by 'Asamis of Patta Mahajan' against enhanced rent, cesses (lags), a new cattle-pound tax 'Bhoonga', externment; signed for 30 villages: Bhograsar, Hindor, Hathusar, Kakralia, Jagor, Chadasar, Bhopalpura, Govindsar, Bakhtawarpura, Hangrasar, Khanisar, Jaswantsar, Bachrara, Ratnisar, Harisinghpura, Rambag, Pipasar, Phalagi, Rampura, Udapur, Bhojusar, Kharya, Surjansar, Ata, Likhmisar, Baladasar, Ranisar, Ramsara, Asrasar, Jagchinpura (list image-verified, PDF p.152). p.10: 'the fief of Mahajan consisted of one hundred and forty villages in the first quarter of the 16th century ... dwindled down to sixty-three villages, fifty-four being in the Patta of Mahajan, and nine in that of Kumbhana'. Text on externed Jat tenants 'of Arsasar, Badher, Ratansar, Kumbhgarh ... all in Patta Mahajan'.
why_relevant: Names at least 8 future range villages (Bhojrasar, Hindor, Hathusar, Kankraliya, Jagor, Khanisar, Rampura, Likhmisar, probably Chidasar) as villages of Patta Mahajan in 1939, with a tenant protest. Pre-1947 social history of the area. Signatories are named (historical, 1939).

title: Gazetteer of the Bikaner State, P.W. Powlett (1874)
what_it_contains: Full text re-OCRed here with tesseract (archive.org's own OCR used a Hindi model and is unusable). Mahajan facts: printed p.86 census table (PDF p.109, image-checked): division 'Mahájan' 69 villages, 1,104 houses, 5,520 population; p.110 (PDF 131): 'Mahajan is about half-way between Bikanir and the Sutlej border; the estate comprises nominally one hundred and forty villages; but of many nothing but their sites remain'; 'Mahajan has been deprived of a third of his estate'; p.124 (PDF 147): 'This estate, containing in 1870 sixty-nine villages belonging to the first thakur of Bikanir, at present is sequestrated' (thakur refused a ten-year lease at Rs 200 per horse for 86 horses); 'Mahajan is seventy miles north-east of Bikanir'. title: Lok Sabha Debates, 2 September 1981, Unstarred Q.2499 (Kumbha Ram Arya): declaration of Mahajan Field Firing Range, Bikaner, as firing and artillery practice range
villages_named: dhannasar (धनसर, village said to be outside the notified area; identification with Dhannasar likely but not certain)
what_it_contains: Statement: Mahajan Range notified under section 9(1) of the Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act 1938, first for five years (OCR: from October 197x), extended to May 1981, then July 1981-June 1986; actual firing notifications Dec 1975-Jun 1976, Dec 1976-Jun 1977, Jul 1977-Jun 1978 etc. Accidents: a civilian of village Dhansar killed while tampering with an 84 mm HEAT rocket at home (no compensation, village outside notified area); night of 23-24 Feb 1981 a house in village Motalai burnt by pyrotechnic ammunition, Rs 7,560 paid on 28 Mar 1981.
why_relevant: Dates the range from 1975 (before land acquisition) and records incidents in Motolai and Dhansar. Names private persons: do not extract.

title: Lok Sabha Debates, 24 August 1984, Unstarred Q.4657: compensation to farmers for losses from firing practice in Rajasthan
what_it_contains: Question refers to 'लूणकरणसर तहसील के 32 गांवों के क्षेत्र में फायरिंग रेंज'. Answer: 'मैनोवर फील्ड फायरिंग एण्ड आर्टिलरी प्रेक्टिस एक्ट 1938 के अधीन अधिसूचित महाजन रेंज नामक एक फील्ड फायरिंग रेंज इस क्षेत्र में 1975 से मौजूद है'; firing about 100 days a year between December and July; cultivation allowed on non-firing days; land to be acquired under the Land Acquisition Act if needed.
why_relevant: In 1984 the number was still 32 villages; confirms the 1975 start of firing before acquisition.
